'''Monica Christine Allanach''' was a British [[actuary]]. She was the first woman to be elected to the Council of the [[Institute of Actuaries]].

==Early life and education==
Allanach's father died when she was four,<ref name="obituary" /> and she was brought up by her widowed mother.<ref name="obituary" /> She was educated at [[Wimbledon High School]] from 1931–1938.<ref name="obituary">{{cite news |last=Fellows |first=Derek |url=https://www.theactuary.com/news/2013/10/obituary-monica-allanach/|work=The Actuary|date=7 November 2013|accessdate=14 November 2019|title=Obituary: Monica Allanach}}</ref><ref name="File">{{cite web |title=File GDS/C: Scrapbook of Monica Allanach, almuna [sic] of Wimbledon High School 1931-1938 |url=https://archive.ioe.ac.uk/DServe/dserve.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27GDS/C%27) |website=Institute of Education, University of London |accessdate=16 November 2019}}</ref> She was good at mathematics at school, and her teachers suggested that she become an actuary.<ref name="Verity">{{cite news |last1=Verity |first1=Christine |title=How to take a seat in the boardroom |url=http://tinyurl.gale.com/tinyurl/CFZZY8 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=The Sunday Telegraph |issue=522 |date=21 February 1971 |location=London, England |page=8}}</ref>

==Career==
Allanach joined the [[Prudential Assurance Company]] in 1938 as an actuarial trainee.<ref name="Shamoon"/> She qualified as an actuary in 1951.<ref name="obituary"/> Women had been permitted to gain membership of the Institute of Actuaries for thirty years, but by 1951, less than one dozen women had become fully qualified.<ref name="obituary"/> Allanach was moved to the male salary scale at Prudential in 1960, several years before the company introduced a single, non-gendered salary scale.<ref name="Shamoon"/> She was appointed as the Deputy Actuary at the Prudential Assurance Company in 1970, thus becoming the first woman to reach management level at the company.<ref name="Shamoon">{{cite news |last1=Shamoon |first1=Stella |title=Woman from the Pru climbs another rung |url=http://tinyurl.gale.com/tinyurl/CFZR38 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=10 October 1970 |location=London, England |page=20}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Business appointments |url=http://tinyurl.gale.com/tinyurl/CFZpj0 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=The Times |issue=57988 |date=5 October 1970 |location=London, England |page=18}}</ref> In 1974 she was promoted to Actuary (UK),<ref>{{cite news |title=Prudential Has New Chief General Manager |url=http://tinyurl.gale.com/tinyurl/CFZmP7 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=Financial Times |issue=26,167 |date=21 September 1973 |location=London, England |page=25}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Appointments. Prudential Assurance |work=Birmingham Daily Post |location=Birmingham, England |date=22 September 1973 |page=5 |url=https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002135/19730922/094/0005 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |via=The British Newspaper Archive}}</ref> and held that position until her retirement in 1981.<ref name="obituary" />

She became a member of the council of the [[Institute of Actuaries]] in 1968, the first woman to be elected to the council.<ref name="obituary" /><ref>{{cite news |title=Appointments. Prudential Assurance |work=Birmingham Daily Post |date=27 June 1968 |page=21 |url=https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002135/19680627/547/0021 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |via=The British Newspaper Archive}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Kamm |first1=Josephine |title=Indicative Past: A Hundred Years of the Girls' Public Day School Trust |date=2013 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=9781134531677 |page=204 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dYJTAQAAQBAJ&dq=%22Monica+Allanach%22&pg=PA204 |accessdate=16 November 2019}}</ref> She was its honorary secretary from 1972 to 1974<ref>{{cite news |title=Appointments. Institute of Actuaries |url=https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002135/19730215/095/0005 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=Birmingham Daily Post |date=15 February 1973 |location=Birmingham, England |page=5 |via=The British Newspaper Archive}}</ref> and its vice-president from 1976 to 1979.<ref name="obituary" /><ref name=allanach>{{cite journal |last1=Allanach |first1=Monica |title=Women Actuaries in the UK |journal=The Actuary |date=May 1982 |volume=16 |issue=5 |pages=4–5 |url=https://www.soa.org/globalassets/assets/library/newsletters/the-actuary/1982/may/act-1982-vol16-iss05-allanach.pdf |accessdate=15 November 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Latest appointments |url=http://tinyurl.gale.com/tinyurl/CFZkD7 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=The Times |issue=60238 |date=16 February 1978 |location=London, England |page=14}}</ref>

In 1977, Allanach was appointed by the [[Secretary of State for Trade]], [[Edmund Dell]], to his panel of insurance advisers.<ref name="obituary" /><ref>{{cite news |title=Insurance post |url=http://tinyurl.gale.com/tinyurl/CFZZv9 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=The Daily Telegraph |issue=37994 |date=26 July 1977 |location=London, England |page=21}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Appointments |url=http://tinyurl.gale.com/tinyurl/CFZhi5 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=Financial Times |issue=27,331 |date=26 July 1977 |location=London, England |page=37}}</ref> She retired from the panel in 1980.<ref>{{cite news |title=Appointments |url=http://tinyurl.gale.com/tinyurl/CFZoM7 |accessdate=16 November 2019 |work=Financial Times |issue=28,232 |date=1 August 1980 |location=London, England |page=21}}</ref>

In 1954 she and Pat Merriman and others began a series of informal meetings, such as tea-parties or wine and cheese parties, for the small minority of women in the profession,<ref name="obituary" /><ref name="gluyas">{{cite news |last1=Gluyas |first1=Andrea |title=Women Actuaries in New Zealand |url=https://actuaries.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/NZSA-May-2016.pdf |accessdate=15 November 2019 |work=President's Newsletter: New Zealand Society of Actuaries |date=May 2016 |page=7}}</ref> from which developed the '''Lady Actuaries Dining Club''' (LADS).<ref name="obituary" /> LADS was wound up in 2011, by which time the Institute of Actuaries had its first woman president, [[Jane Curtis]].<ref name="pryor">{{cite web |last1=Pryor |first1=Louise |title=Inspired by Ada Lovelace |url=https://www.louisepryor.com/2011/11/07/inspired-by-ada-lovelace/ |accessdate=15 November 2019 |date=7 November 2011}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*{{cite journal |last1=Allanach |first1=Monica |title=Women Actuaries in the UK |journal=The Actuary |date=May 1982 |volume=16 |issue=5 |pages=4–5 |url=https://www.soa.org/globalassets/assets/library/newsletters/the-actuary/1982/may/act-1982-vol16-iss05-allanach.pdf |accessdate=15 November 2019}}

==Legacy==
Allanach's writing, including a 1964 paper 'The treatment of expenses in the calculation of ordinary branch premiums', was required reading for exams at the Institute of Actuaries.<ref name="obituary" /> In 2015, the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries held a Monica Allanach lecture.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cooper |first1=Deborah |title=Bias busting |journal=The Actuary |date=October 2015 |page=9 |url=https://issuu.com/redactive/docs/act_oct15_full_lr |accessdate=16 November 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Allanach was a member of the Friends of the [[Girls' Public Day School Trust]], serving as its Honorary Treasurer from 1962–1972.<ref name="obituary" /><ref name="File"/> She lived near Wimbledon, and had a keen interest in tennis.<ref name="obituary" /><ref name="Shamoon"/> She did not marry, and believed that she would not have been promoted to senior positions had she done so.<ref name="Verity"/> In July 1981, she was made a [[Freeman of the City of London]].<ref name="obituary" />
